name: India DPDP Act
description: India Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 — data-fiduciary security obligations (paraphrased).

controls.title: Consent management
controls.description: Personal data is processed on the basis of free, specific, informed consent that can be withdrawn.

checks.rationale: Consent mechanism documentation is the direct artifact.

controls.title: General obligations of the data fiduciary
Accuracy and completeness of personal data
Technical and organisational measures
controls.description: A data fiduciary implements appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure effective observance of the Act.
controls.evidence_guidance: Security policies plus operating technical controls.

checks.rationale: Organisational measures require a published, acknowledged security policy.
Continuous scanning schedules evidence operating technical measures.

controls.title: Security safeguards to prevent breach
controls.description: Reasonable security safeguards are implemented to prevent personal data breach.
controls.evidence_guidance: Vulnerability management operating: scans, remediation, no open criticals.

checks.rationale: Regular vulnerability scanning is a reasonable safeguard against breach.

controls.title: Breach intimation
controls.description: On personal data breach, the Board and each affected data principal are informed in the prescribed manner.

checks.rationale: A documented procedure for Board/principal notification is the readiness artifact.
Notification executes through the IR program.

controls.title: Erasure when purpose is served or consent withdrawn
Significant data fiduciary — DPIA & audit
controls.description: Significant data fiduciaries undertake periodic data protection impact assessment and audit.
controls.evidence_guidance: Periodic risk/impact assessments and independent reviews.

checks.rationale: Independent testing supports the periodic audit obligation.

controls.title: Right to access information about personal data
